newsitem.title: NORWAY: SOCCER-SOLSKJAER SAVES NORWAY FROM EMBARRASSING DEFEAT.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SOLSKJAER SAVES NORWAY FROM EMBARRASSING DEFEAT.

text.p: Manchester United's Ole Gunnar Solskjaer saved Norway from an embarrassing World Cup defeat by Finland with an 83rd minute goal in their group three qualifier on Wednesday.
The 1-1 draw kept Norway at the top of the group with 10 points from four matches. They are four clear of second placed Switzerland who beat Hungary 1-0 in Zurich and six ahead of Finland.
Norway dominated in the first half but fell behind on the hour to a goal by Antti Sumiala.
The Finns, known for their robust rearguard, then defended in depth until Solskjaer's late strike as some intense pressure finally paid off.
There was controversy as early as the second minute when Solskjaer seemed to have scored from five metres out with a fierce shot that sent Finnish goalkeeper Antti Niemi backwards inside his goal.
But Niemi succeeded in holding onto the ball and the referee ruled it had not crossed the line -- to loud protests from the 22,300-strong crowd at Oslo's Ullevaal stadium.
"This is a psychological boost," Finland's Danish coach Richad Moeller Nielsen said. "Not many teams walk away with one point here at Ullevaal."
"It was an important point for us, but we are in a difficult situation (in the standings). It does, however, give the players more confidence for the next matches."
Norwegian coach Egil "Drillo" Olsen said: "All in all I am
very disappointed we lost two points. None of our players did very well but nobody was particularly bad either."
Asked about Norway's chances of reaching the 1998 finals in France, Olsen said: "The chances are probably still more than 50 percent."
Olsen had rated Norway's chances at 80 percent before Wednesday's lacklustre match.
